raw_response:
I will keep my plan conservative and labor-saving because I am 58, my family has some off-farm work, and I only have 12.4 mu, so I care more about steady output and manageable fieldwork than chasing the highest possible yield. I will still make cotton my main crop because that matches my usual system and my experience is strongest there. I will spread some land into wheat, maize, mung bean, and peanut so I do not put everything into one crop, and so I can balance cash income, food grain, soil use, and labor across the year. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages instead of watering too often. I will not use excessive fertilizer because that raises cost and can cause weak growth, lodging, or waste. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand establishment and yield stability, and I will choose tillage based on what is practical for each crop: more thorough land preparation for cotton and peanut, and simpler rotary tillage for the grain crops. I will also keep pesticide use moderate, only enough to protect yield, because too many applications cost money and add work.
